hero_question.reason: The hero shows six months of income against spending with what is left each month (averaging CHF 250.82, several months negative), directly answering Jana's stated question of why so little is left at the end of the month now that she earns well.

about_customer.reason: Every tile reflects her real situation — the month-end shortfall, the CHF 150 monthly repayment to her mother, her emergency fund at 49.2%, the provisional tax bill that surprised her, and her actual rent, health insurance and fitness payments due — with no generic filler and nothing belonging to another kind of customer (no investments or credit-card content she doesn't have).

titles.reason: Titles like "In and out", "Paying back parents" and "Bills due soon" are short, read like a person wrote them, use her own terms (paying back parents, emergency fund, tax bill) and match exactly what each tile shows.

not_empty_or_repeated.reason: All tiles carry real, non-zero figures, and the tax bill standing beside the bills-due list it belongs to is the sanctioned pattern of showing one bill's detail (here its provisional flag) next to the list, not a duplicate in different words.

coherent.reason: The board tells one story a customer would follow — what comes in and goes out each month, the commitments coming due soon (parents, tax, rent, insurance), and the buffer she is building — which fits its name "What's left" and her core concern about what she can afford.
